title: Kinetic Theory of Gases and Radiation
subject: Physics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Quick Revision

nodes.title: Ideal Gas Laws & Kinetic Postulates
points: Gas laws: Boyle's law (P ∝ 1/V at const T), Charles' law (V ∝ T at const P), Gay-Lussac's law (P ∝ T at const V).
Ideal gas equation of state: PV = nRT = N k_B T, where k_B = R/N_A = 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J/K is Boltzmann's constant.
Assumptions of kinetic theory: gas consists of tiny identical point particles in random continuous motion.
Intermolecular forces are negligible except during collisions; collisions are perfectly elastic.
Time of collision is negligible compared to time between successive collisions; volume of gas molecules is negligible compared to container volume.

nodes.title: Pressure of an Ideal Gas & Kinetic Interpretation of T
points: Derivation of gas pressure: P = ⅓ ρ v_rms² = ⅓ (Nm/V) v_rms².
Kinetic interpretation of temperature: Absolute temperature T is directly proportional to the average translational KE of molecules.
Average translational KE per molecule: E_mol = 3/2 k_B T (independent of the nature of the gas, depends only on T).
Average translational KE per mole: E_mole = 3/2 RT.
At absolute zero (T = 0 K), molecular motion completely ceases and v_rms = 0.

formulas.label: Pressure formula
formulas.expr: P = ⅓ ρ v_rms² = ⅓ (Nm/V) v_rms²

nodes.title: Molecular Speeds: RMS, Average & Most Probable
points: RMS speed: v_rms = √(3RT / M₀) = √(3k_B T / m) = √(3P / ρ).
Average speed: v_avg = √(8RT / πM₀) ≈ 0.92 v_rms.
Most probable speed: v_mp = √(2RT / M₀) ≈ 0.816 v_rms.
Order of speeds: v_rms > v_avg > v_mp (Remember: 'RAM' ⟹ RMS > Average > Most Probable).
Ratio of speeds: v_mp : v_avg : v_rms = √2 : √(8/π) : √3 ≈ 1 : 1.128 : 1.224.
Speed is directly proportional to √T and inversely proportional to √M₀.

nodes.title: Degrees of Freedom & Law of Equipartition
points: Degree of freedom (f): number of independent coordinates or quadratic terms required to specify the dynamical state of a molecule.
Law of equipartition of energy: Energy associated with each degree of freedom per molecule is ½ k_B T.
Monoatomic gas (He, Ne, Ar): f = 3 (all translational), total internal energy U = 3/2 N k_B T.
Diatomic gas rigid rotator (O₂, N₂, H₂ at normal T): f = 5 (3 translational + 2 rotational), U = 5/2 N k_B T.
Diatomic gas with vibration (at high T): f = 7 (3 trans + 2 rot + 2 vibrational modes: 1 KE + 1 PE), U = 7/2 N k_B T.

nodes.title: Molar Specific Heats & Mayer's Relation
points: Molar specific heat at constant volume C_v = dU/dT = (f/2)R; at constant pressure C_p = C_v + R = (f/2 + 1)R.
Mayer's Relation: C_p − C_v = R (in molar units) or C_p − C_v = R/J (in heat units, cal/mol·K).
For principal specific heats (per gram): S_p − S_v = R/(M₀ J).
Adiabatic ratio γ = C_p / C_v = 1 + 2/f.
Monoatomic: C_v = 3/2 R, C_p = 5/2 R, γ = 5/3 = 1.67.
Diatomic (rigid): C_v = 5/2 R, C_p = 7/2 R, γ = 7/5 = 1.40.
Diatomic (vibrating): C_v = 7/2 R, C_p = 9/2 R, γ = 9/7 = 1.28.

nodes.title: Mean Free Path & Molecular Collisions
points: Mean free path λ is the average distance traversed by a gas molecule between two successive collisions.
Formula: λ = 1 / (√2 π n d²), where n = N/V is number density and d is molecular diameter.
In terms of P and T: λ = k_B T / (√2 π d² P).
Dependence: λ ∝ T (at constant P); λ ∝ 1/P (at constant T); λ ∝ 1/ρ (independent of T at constant V).
Collision frequency = v_avg / λ.

formulas.label: λ in terms of P & T
formulas.expr: λ = k_B T / (√2 π d² P)

nodes.title: Thermal Radiation & Ferry's Blackbody
points: Radiant energy incident on a surface: Q = Q_a + Q_r + Q_t ⟹ a + r + t = 1.
Coefficients: absorptive power a = Q_a/Q, reflective power r = Q_r/Q, transmissive power t = Q_t/Q.
Athermanous body (t = 0 ⟹ a + r = 1, e.g., wood, iron); Diathermanous body (t ≠ 0, e.g., glass, quartz).
Perfect blackbody absorbs all incident radiant energy (a = 1, r = 0, t = 0).
Ferry's Blackbody: Double-walled evacuated hollow sphere coated with lampblack inside, with a small aperture and conical projection opposite the hole to ensure multiple internal reflections.

nodes.title: Kirchhoff's, Wien's & Stefan-Boltzmann Laws
points: Kirchhoff's Law of Radiation: At thermal equilibrium, the emissivity of a body equals its absorptive power (e = a). Good absorbers are good emitters.
Wien's Displacement Law: Wavelength corresponding to maximum radiant intensity is inversely proportional to absolute temperature: λ_max × T = b (Wien's constant b = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K).
Stefan-Boltzmann Law: Total radiant power emitted per unit area of a blackbody is directly proportional to fourth power of absolute temperature: R_b = σT⁴.
Stefan's constant: σ = 5.67 × 10⁻⁸ W/(m²·K⁴). Dimensions: [M¹L⁰T⁻³K⁻⁴].
For an ordinary body of emissivity e in surroundings at temperature T₀: Net radiant power loss R_net = e σ (T⁴ − T₀⁴).

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Definitions
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive gas pressure P = ⅓ ρ v_rms² from kinetic theory assumptions.
Board Favourite #2: Prove Mayer's relation C_p − C_v = R using First Law of Thermodynamics.
Board Favourite #3: Draw and explain Ferry's perfectly blackbody with neat labeled diagram.
Board Favourite #4: State and prove Kirchhoff's law of radiation theoretically.
Definitions to Master: Mean free path, Emissive power, Emissivity, Coefficient of absorption, Wien's displacement law.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Traps, Shortcuts & Speed Formulas
points: Stefan's Law Ratio Trap: Radiant power ratio E₁/E₂ = (T₁/T₂)⁴. Always convert temperatures to KELVIN (K = °C + 273)!
Small Temperature Rise Shortcut: If T increases by x% (where x < 5%), radiant power E increases by ≈ 4x%.
Wien's Law Shortcut: λ₁ T₁ = λ₂ T₂. If temperature doubles, peak wavelength is halved (shifts towards blue/UV).
RMS Speed Shortcut: v₁/v₂ = √(T₁/T₂) × √(M₂/M₁). When temperature quadruples, RMS speed doubles.
Mixture of Non-Reacting Gases: n_total = n₁ + n₂; C_v(mix) = (n₁C_v1 + n₂C_v2)/(n₁ + n₂); γ(mix) = C_p(mix)/C_v(mix).
Trap: Energy per mole depends only on temperature (E = 3/2 RT for monoatomic), NOT on pressure or volume.
